relationships.subject: Rapamycin
relationships.evidence_quote: Both thresholds of mechanical allodynia (Figure 3B, upper) and thermal hyperalgesia (Figure 3B, down) decreased with the inhibition of autophagy and increased with the activation of autophagy

relationships.subject: Autophagy
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, the TRAF6 protein level in spinal cord was also decreased by activating autophagy

relationships.subject: TRAF6
relationships.evidence_quote: inhibition of TRAF6 expression by Traf6 siRNA treatment reversed the increase of p-MAPK8 and NFKB levels induced by autophagy inhibition

relationships.subject: Autophagy
relationships.evidence_quote: Levels of neuroinflammatory factors, including IL1B, TNF, CCL7, and MMP2 were increased by inhibition of autophagy and decreased by induction of autophagy

relationships.subject: NF-kB
relationships.evidence_quote: inhibition of the MAPK8 or NFKB pathway (P < 0.01), rather than the MAPK14 or MAPK1 pathway (P > 0.05), markedly decreased expression levels of CCL7 and MMP2 after autophagy inhibition

key_findings: Autophagy flux is impaired mainly in spinal astrocytes during neuropathic pain maintenance; inhibiting autophagy aggravates pain and activating relieves it
Impaired autophagy raises neuroinflammation via TRAF6-K63 ubiquitin binding, MAPK8 and NF-kB; NRF2 activation improves astrocyte glutathione and pain relief
